chicken-breast-baked-or-broiled-skin-not.title: Chicken breast, baked or broiled, skin not eaten, from pre-cooked

content.title: About
content.content: Skinless chicken breast is a lean source of protein obtained after cooking (baking or broiling) a pre‑cooked product. It contains very little fat, high‑quality protein, and important micronutrients such as vitamin B6, niacin, phosphorus and selenium.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken breast is the leanest cut of chicken, containing less than 2 g of fat per 100 g.
Dry‑heat cooking without skin retains most B‑vitamins, which are crucial for metabolism.
Poultry is considered “white meat,” which is generally easier to digest than red meat.
Breast meat is a staple in diet plans, sports nutrition, and low‑calorie recipes.
When baked without added fat, the breast stays moist and tender due to its natural juices.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Approximately 31 g of protein per 100 g supports muscle growth, repair, and satiety.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Less than 2 g of fat per 100 g makes it suitable for low‑fat dietary patterns.

items.title: Vitamin B6 and niacin
items.content: These B‑vitamins aid in protein and carbohydrate metabolism and support nervous system function.

items.title: Selenium
items.content: Selenium acts as an antioxidant, helping protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Phosphorus
items.content: Phosphorus is essential for bone health and cellular energy processes.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Insufficient cooking may leave pathogenic bacteria; ensure the product is fully cooked.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Sodium content in processed product
items.content: Pre‑cooked versions can contain added salt; people monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chicken breast can be served hot, diced into salads, added to soups, used in low‑carb wraps, or sliced thin and quickly pan‑seared without oil. It pairs well with vegetables, whole grains, or healthy fats.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked chicken breast in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3–4 days. For longer storage, freeze it in a zip‑top bag; thaw in the refrigerator rather than at room temperature.

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken wings coated in a hot sauce are a popular snack often served in bars and restaurants. The wings are typically fried or baked and then tossed in a sauce made from chili peppers, vinegar, sugar and spices, giving them a bright, spicy‑sweet flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wings are sometimes called "the roll‑up" because of their shape.
Hot sauces can contain over 30 varieties of pepper, from jalapeño to habanero.
U.S. consumption of chicken wings has increased more than five‑fold since the 1990s.
Traditionally wings are served with blue‑cheese or ranch dressing.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 supports amino‑acid metabolism and nervous‑system function.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc is important for immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Wings fit well into low‑carb diets when not paired with sugary sauces.

items.title: Antioxidants in the sauce
items.content: Chili peppers contain capsaicin, which has anti‑inflammatory and thermogenic properties.

items.title: Spicy sauce may irritate the stomach
items.content: People with sensitive stomachs or gastritis may experience discomfort after eating very hot foods.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have an allergic reaction to chicken meat.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Sauces often contain a lot of salt; those with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Fried wings and sauce can be calorie‑rich, so portion control is important.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Wings are served hot, usually in individual portions. They are eaten with the hands, pulling the meat off the bone, or with a fork. Common accompaniments include celery sticks and blue‑cheese dressing.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked wings in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a bag at –18 °C; thaw in the fridge before reheating.

egg-substitute-omelet-scrambled-or-fried.title: Egg substitute, omelet, scrambled, or fried with vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: Egg substitute is a ready‑made blend, usually based on plant proteins, starches and food additives, that allows you to make an omelet, scrambled eggs or fried dishes with vegetables without using real eggs. It is popular in vegan and vegetarian diets and for people with egg allergies.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The mix often contains pea or soy protein that mimics the structure of egg white.
Turmeric or food coloring is added to give a yellow hue similar to eggs.
It can be used in baking, sauces and even desserts, typically at a 1:1 ratio with eggs.
Some brands fortify the product with vitamins B12 and D, important for vegans.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: The blend provides a high amount of protein needed for tissue repair and muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low in cholesterol
items.content: Unlike real eggs, the product contains no cholesterol, which is beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Fortified versions supply vitamin B12, which is usually missing from plant‑based diets.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Starch and added fiber help maintain normal bowel function.

items.title: Allergy‑friendly
items.content: Absence of egg protein makes it safe for those with egg allergies.

items.title: Soy or pea protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to the protein sources used in the substitute.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Certain brands add salt for flavor, so sodium intake should be monitored.

items.title: Does not fully replace yolk
items.content: For dishes where yolk texture and flavor are crucial, the substitute may fall short.

items.title: Processed ingredients
items.content: The product can contain additives and preservatives that may not suit everyone.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Mix the powder with water (usually 1:1) until smooth, then cook in a lightly oiled pan, adding your favorite vegetables – tomatoes, spinach, bell pepper, mushrooms. For an omelet, cook like a regular one; for scrambled, stir continuously; for fried, let it set without stirring until a crust forms.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in a sealed container. After opening, use within 4–6 weeks. Discard if you notice off‑odors or discoloration.

fruit-salad-including-citrus-fruit-with-.title: Fruit Salad with Citrus and Whipped Cream

content.title: About
content.content: Fruit salad with citrus and whipped cream is a mix of fresh fruits such as oranges, grapefruits, mandarins and lime, tossed with light, airy whipped cream. The balance of sweet and tangy makes it a refreshing dessert suitable for any season.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Citrus fruits are rich in vitamin C, which supports the immune system.
Whipped cream is usually made from heavy cream with at least 30 % fat.
Fruit salads are often served in chilled glasses to keep them fresh.
The combination of sour and sweet flavors enhances aroma perception.
Traditionally fruit salads are served at holidays and family celebrations.

items.title: High in vitamin C
items.content: Citrus fruits provide a high amount of vitamin C, a powerful antioxidant that supports skin health.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from the fruits aids regular bowel movements and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports normal blood pressure.

items.title: Low‑calorie dessert
items.content: When made with a moderate amount of cream, the fruit salad remains a relatively low‑calorie sweet option.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Citrus flavonoids contribute to improved vascular function.

items.title: Citrus allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to citrus, including itching, swelling or rash.

items.title: High natural sugar
items.content: Fruits are naturally sweet; people with diabetes should consider the glycemic impact.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The acidity of citrus can irritate sensitive teeth or the stomach if consumed in excess.

items.title: Cream and lactose intolerance
items.content: Those with lactose intolerance should use lactose‑free cream or dairy‑free alternatives.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled, garnished with mint leaves or berries. It can be enjoyed as a standalone dessert, added to pancakes, or used as a filling for cakes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Cream may separate, so gently stir before serving.

infant-formula-similac-alimentum-powder-.title: Similac Alimentum Powder, Ready-to-Mix with Water

content.title: About
content.content: Similac Alimentum is a hypoallergenic infant formula powder designed for babies with heightened sensitivity to cow‑milk proteins. It contains partially hydrolyzed protein, prebiotics, and essential vitamins and minerals. Preparation is simple: just add clean water.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Similac Alimentum is specifically formulated for infants diagnosed with cow‑milk protein allergy and other food sensitivities.
The formula uses partially hydrolyzed protein, which reduces the risk of allergic reactions.
Prebiotic fibers (FOS) are included to support a healthy gut microbiome.
The product has undergone clinical testing and is approved by pediatricians in over 30 countries.
One container yields about 800 ml of ready‑to‑feed formula (approximately 30 servings).

items.title: Supports growth and development
items.content: Provides all essential macro‑ and micronutrients—including protein, fat, carbohydrates, vitamins D, A, C, and minerals such as calcium, iron, and zinc—for normal infant growth.

items.title: Reduces allergy risk
items.content: Partially hydrolyzed protein is less allergenic, helping to lessen symptoms in sensitive infants.

items.title: Gut health support
items.content: Prebiotic fibers promote the growth of beneficial bacteria, improving digestion and nutrient absorption.

items.title: Immune system support
items.content: Vitamins A, C, and zinc play key roles in maintaining a healthy immune response in babies.

items.title: Soy lecithin allergy
items.content: The formula contains soy lecithin, which may trigger reactions in infants allergic to soy.

items.title: Improper mixing
items.content: Using too much or too little water can lead to dehydration or inadequate nutrition.

items.title: Shelf‑life after opening
items.content: Once opened, the powder should be used within 48 hours and kept refrigerated.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Mix the specified amount of powder with clean water (37 °C), stir thoroughly until smooth. The prepared formula should be fed immediately and used within 30 minutes of preparation.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the powder refrigerated and consume within 48 hours.

content.title: About
content.content: Orange Blossom (5400) is an aromatic extract obtained from the flowers of the orange tree (Citrus sinensis). It features a bright, fresh citrus scent with sweet floral nuances. Used in culinary arts, perfumery, and aromatherapy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Orange blossoms are hand‑picked in early spring when fully open.
The extract is produced by steam distillation, preserving its natural aroma.
Traditionally used in Mediterranean cuisine to flavor desserts, drinks, and sauces.
In perfumery, it is one of the most versatile and long‑lasting notes, often blended with bergamot and jasmine.
The scent is considered calming and stress‑relieving.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Flavonoids in the extract help neutralize free radicals, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Calming effect
items.content: The aroma is frequently used in aromatherapy to reduce anxiety and improve mood.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: Small amounts may stimulate gastric juice production, aiding digestion.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to citrus aromatic compounds.

items.title: Photosensitivity
items.content: Topical use in high concentrations can increase skin sensitivity to UV light.

items.title: Pregnancy and breastfeeding
items.content: Safety of internal consumption in large amounts during pregnancy is not established; consult a healthcare professional.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Add a few drops of the extract to dough, creams, ice cream, or cocktails for a vivid citrus flavor. In perfumery, incorporate it as a top, middle, or base note. For aromatherapy, dilute in a diffuser or carrier oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a tightly sealed dark bottle at room temperature, away from direct sunlight. For extended shelf life, keep refrigerated. Typical shelf life is 2–3 years.
